messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: ACME trial: procurement & commercial path — post-call recap

Hi Jordan / team,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion on the pilot goals and success criteria. Below is a quick recap and proposed next steps to make sure the trial can convert smoothly to paid if we hit the agreed thresholds.

Recap from today's call:
- Trial scope: 30-day pilot, 5 seats, API access for search-ranking and chat features.
- Success criteria: sustained inference volume of ~100k tokens/day or 10k embeddings/day for 7 consecutive days + product team sign-off on latency and quality.
- Data & security: ACME requested SOC 2 report, SCIM/SAML for SSO considered later in the project.

Procurement / commercial path questions:
1) Payment method: Will ACME use a PO (net 30) or corporate card for initial billing?
2) Marketplace: Any interest in purchasing via AWS Marketplace (may simplify procurement and invoices)?
3) Invoicing: Who is the AP contact and where should invoices be sent?
4) Contracting: Are you planning to route through procurement/legal first or can we start with a simple MSA + PO?

Next steps (proposed):
- If ACME will use a PO, please share the PO template + AP contact and we’ll return vendor info and insurance details.
- If using card or marketplace, we can start billing as soon as we hit conversion triggers (we can define triggers below).
- I’ll attach our PO/vendor info and the standard security questionnaire for your team.

Trial-to-paid conversion suggestion (to discuss):
- Option A (automatic billing): If trial usage exceeds 100k tokens/day or 10k embeddings/day for 7 consecutive days within the trial window, we start billing under the agreed committed rate beginning the following billing period.
- Option B (manual sign-off): Product + Procurement sign-off required to move to paid.

Please loop in procurement/legal as needed — copying Vivek for any contract/discount questions. I’ll follow up with our SOC 2 attestation and the vendor packet in a separate email.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few notes from our side:

1) Payment method: For pilots of this size Procurement prefers a PO (net 30). For smaller proofs of concept they sometimes allow a corporate card but given the volume we expect this to be a PO.
2) Marketplace: We prefer invoices but would consider AWS Marketplace if pricing/terms align — will need procurement input.
3) AP contact: procurement@acmecorp.com (cc'd) — invoices go to AP team, please include our PO number when provided.
4) Contracting: We'll need a short vendor form + standard MSA. Ashley from Legal is cc'd and will review the MSA and any redlines.

I’m attaching our standard PO template and the procurement intake form. Procurement team — can you confirm turnaround for processing a vendor (timeline / required docs)?

Jordan

Subject: Vendor onboarding / PO details for Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the thread. A few items we need to onboard Redwood as a vendor and process a PO:
- W9 or equivalent (for US vendors)
- Vendor packet (insurance certificates, tax ID, contact for invoices)
- Signed MSA or acceptance of standard terms (we can accept via DocuSign)
- SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent security attestation (if available)

Please send the vendor packet and SOC 2 report. If you have a standard MSA we can review and route to legal. Typical processing time: ~7–10 business days after we receive a complete packet and SOC 2.

AP contact for invoices: ap.payables@acmecorp.com
Please include the PO number on the invoice once issued.

Regards,

Subject: Re: ACME trial: procurement & commercial path — next steps & conversion triggers

Appreciate the quick responses — looping in a few concrete next steps to keep momentum:

1) Deliverables from Redwood (I’ll attach these in a follow-up):
   - Vendor packet (W9, insurance, tax id)
   - SOC 2 Type II summary and attestation link
   - Standard MSA (we can accept minor redlines)
2) Procurement intake: Please confirm expected PO turnaround so we can align trial start/billing window.
3) Conversion triggers: We recommend using Option A (automatic billing) as a default for speed to value, but we’re happy to make this manual sign-off if ACME prefers. Suggested definition we can agree to now:
   - If trial usage reaches either 100,000 tokens/day OR 10,000 embeddings/day sustained for 7 consecutive days within the 30-day pilot, Redwood will notify ACME and transition to billing at the agreed committed rate starting the first day after the trigger period.

If Procurement prefers to delay billing until a signed PO is in place, we can mark the trial as “conversion-pending PO” and hold billing until the PO is issued (we’ll set a 14-day window for issuance after the trigger to avoid blocking).

Marketplace note: We’re happy to pursue AWS Marketplace if that would accelerate procurement. Vivek, can you share a quick note on whether the deal would benefit from a marketplace listing?

Vivek Kulkarni (cc): Vivek, can you confirm if any price or discount approvals are needed now? Also, we have deal record DEAL-ACME-4721 in HubSpot.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the vendor packet and SOC 2 link this afternoon.
